sections.h2: Is Newburgh a town or a city, and why does it matter when selling?
sections.html:
There are two Newburghs in Orange County, and the Census figures used on this page describe the town. The city of Newburgh, a separate municipality on the river, was part of the town until it was rechartered in 1865. Since then it has been fully independent, independent of the town.

In 2020 the town had 31,985 residents and the city and town together had 60,842. The town passed the city in population for the first time in the 2010 census. If your deed or tax bill says Newburgh, confirm which municipality issued it before you look up dates and rules.

The rest of this page covers the town: its land, its tax calendar, its school districts and the offices a seller deals with.

sections.h2: What is the land like in the town of Newburgh?
sections.html:
The town covers 43.36 square miles of land, hilly in the middle and bounded on the east by the Hudson River. Steep bluffs line most of the shoreline, so very few houses have easy river access. The northern line and about a third of the western line touch Ulster County.

Several hills top 750 feet. Cronomer Hill, at 725 feet, is the central landmark, and most of it is a county-owned park with an observation tower that looks toward the Newburgh-Beacon Bridge and Stewart Airport. On hilly lots like these, a survey and a look at drainage are worth doing before you list.

Named areas include Balmville, Gardnertown, Orange Lake, Fostertown and Algonquin Park, home to the town's only historic district built around old gunpowder mills. Newburgh is also one of eight towns in Orange County with no incorporated villages inside it.

sections.h2: What is the history behind the Newburgh town name and its farmland?
sections.html:
German Palatine refugees settled the area in 1709 under the name Neuburg, and Scottish immigrants soon joined them. The area became a precinct in 1762 and a town in 1788. When Rockland County was cut from Orange in 1798, Newburgh and other southern Ulster towns were moved into Orange County.

The town stayed rural into the twentieth century, with apple orchards in the north and dairy and vegetable farms elsewhere. The postwar years turned farmland into subdivisions and school sites. Some of that history is still visible today: the PepsiCo bottling plant stands where a Little League ballpark once did, and Wedgewood Park, planned in the 1960s, was not finished until the late 1980s.

Expect a spread of ages in the housing stock, from farmhouses to 1980s developments.

sections.h2: What do the roads and the airport do for house values in Newburgh?
sections.html:
The town calls itself the "Crossroads of the Northeast," and the map backs it up: Interstate 84 runs east to west, the New York State Thruway (I-87) runs north to south, and a direct ramp between the two opened in December 2009. Route 300 is the main commercial strip, with Routes 9W, 17K, 32, 52 and 207 also crossing the town.

Stewart International Airport sits partly in the town, though mostly in New Windsor, and much of the land around it became Stewart State Forest. Most roads are maintained by the town highway department, two are county roads, and the town also has many private roads. If your house is on a private road, ask who plows and repairs it before you list.

The Census Bureau lists 2022 retail sales per capita at $37,920 in the town, above New Rochelle ($19,931) and New Windsor ($11,352) and close to New York City ($20,303).

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show about Newburgh homes and buyers?
sections.html:
Newburgh is a town of owners, with 79.8 percent of homes owner-occupied. The Census Bureau puts the median home value at $375,700 and median gross rent at $2,159 for 2020 to 2024, which is higher rent than in New Windsor next door.

  • Households: 11,640, with 2.71 people each
  • Median household income: $111,615 in 2024 dollars
  • Poverty rate: 7.3 percent
  • Estimated population change since 2020: down 0.5 percent
  • Mean commute: 36.6 minutes

The 2022 business figures show $1,207,597,000 in retail sales, $196,134,000 in transportation and warehousing receipts and $148,831,000 in health care and social assistance revenue for the town.

Most residents have lived in the same house for years. The Census shows 93.1 percent in the same home one year earlier, so few households move in any given year.

sections.h2: Who bills me for taxes in Newburgh, and what are the key dates?
sections.html:
The Receiver of Taxes bills property tax, but school tax depends on your district, because four of them serve the town: Marlboro, Wallkill, Valley Central and the Newburgh Enlarged City School District. Who collects the school bill depends on the district:

  • Marlboro: the town Receiver collects it
  • Valley Central: the town Receiver collects it
  • Wallkill: the district's own tax collector
  • Newburgh Enlarged City School District: the district's own tax collector
DateTown of Newburgh assessment or billing step
March 1Taxable status date and exemption filing deadline
May 1Tentative roll and assessment change notices
Fourth Tuesday in MayGrievance Day
July 1Final assessment roll filed
SeptemberMarlboro and Valley Central school tax due without penalty
OctoberSame school taxes carry a 2 percent penalty
JanuaryFull property tax bill due without penalty

Source: Town of Newburgh Assessor and Receiver of Taxes pages. The town has 13,027 taxable parcels.

The Receiver does not allow partial payments or installments on property tax. Water and sewer bills come four times a year, with a 5 percent penalty after 30 days, and unpaid amounts are added to the next year's property tax bill. That last rule is worth knowing: a water balance can land on the property's next tax bill unless it is settled at closing.

sections.h2: What offices handle exemptions, permits and the deed?
sections.html:
The Assessor handles exemptions, including STAR, veterans, senior citizen, disability and agricultural ones. Ask the office which of them are on your parcel. Its page links the state's Basic and Enhanced STAR credit registration and forms for the alternative veterans, Cold War veterans, low-income disability and senior citizen exemptions. The Code Compliance Department issues building permits and certificates of occupancy for new and existing structures and investigates code complaints.

The deed itself is recorded with the Orange County Clerk, and the state transfer tax return, Form TP-584, goes to the same office within 15 days after the deed is delivered. The state tax is $2 for each $500 of price, and by default the seller pays it. The Clerk says a copy of your deed costs about $5 directly from the office, so avoid third-party companies that charge more.

When a cash buyer takes the house as-is, the same paperwork still applies. Closing the file with the clerk and settling water, sewer and tax balances is what finishes the sale.

faqs.q: Is the Census population on this page for the town or the city of Newburgh?
faqs.a: It is for the town, which the Census Bureau estimates at 31,825 residents in 2025. The city of Newburgh is a separate municipality and is not included in that figure.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in the town of Newburgh?
faqs.a: The fourth Tuesday in May. The tentative roll comes out May 1, and the final roll is filed July 1.

faqs.q: Who collects school tax in the town of Newburgh?
faqs.a: It depends on the district. The town's Receiver collects for Marlboro and Valley Central, while Wallkill and the Newburgh Enlarged City School District use their own collectors.

faqs.q: Can I pay Newburgh property tax in installments?
faqs.a: No. The Receiver says installments and partial payments are not allowed for property tax, so the January amount is the full bill, and penalties start if you pay in February or March.

faqs.q: Do unpaid water bills affect a Newburgh house sale?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid water and sewer bills are added to the next year's property tax bill, so settle them at or before closing.
